I need the front end for Commonroom Check-in. The sign-in and membership registration system on the front-desk kiosk of a neighborhood community center, used by visitors to join and sign in to drop-in programs and by the volunteer at the desk who helps them.

Who's using it: Doreen Mitchell, 68, a recently widowed retiree visiting the center for the first time to join the Tuesday knitting circle. She is filling in the form herself at the kiosk while Raj, a volunteer, stands beside her and a short line of regulars waits to sign in behind her.

What they're doing right now: Doreen is partway through the new-member form. She has entered her name, address and phone number. The phone number was rejected because she included the area code twice. The system has also flagged that a member record from 2019 exists for 'Doreen Kowalski' at the same address, which is her maiden name from when she took a pottery class. She and Raj need to decide whether to update the old record or create a new one, fix the phone number, add an emergency contact, answer the photo-consent question and finish so she can sign in to today's 10:00 session.

What's in the system at this point: Center membership: 1,240 active members and 3,100 lapsed records. New-member form sections: name and any previous names, address, phone (10 digits), email (optional), date of birth (used for age-group programs), emergency contact name, relationship and phone, accessibility needs (optional), photo consent for the newsletter (yes or no), and how they heard about the center. Possible match: member #04417 'Doreen Kowalski', same street address, phone on file ending 3391, last visit April 2019, pottery class. Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
